events.description: Brzezinski memo to President on Soviet intervention in Afghanistan, recommending aid to rebels, reassurance of Pakistan, Chinese and Islamic cooperation.
Soviet intervention in Afghanistan, described as extremely grave challenge.

Brzezinski sends the memorandum 'Reflections on Soviet Intervention in Afghanistan' to President Carter, recommending support for the Afghan rebels, reassurance of Pakistan, and engagement of China and Islamic countries.
Soviet military intervention in Afghanistan, prompting a regional crisis alongside turmoil in Iran.
NSC meeting scheduled for Friday focusing on Afghanistan and Iran, with an agenda to be sent.
Special Coordination Committee meets on Afghanistan and Iran; minutes sent to the President.
Planned Harold Brown visit to China, whose substance would be influenced by the Soviet intervention.

relationships.detail: Memorandum to the President from his national security adviser.
relationships.quote: MEMORANDUM FOR: THE PRESIDENT FROM: ZBIGNIEW BRZEZINSKI

relationships.detail: Resistance opposing Soviet intervention; memo recommends supporting it.
relationships.quote: It is essential that Afghanistani resistance continues. This means more money as well as arms shipments to the rebels

relationships.detail: Memo urges encouraging Pakistan to help the rebels; Pakistan hosts 300,000 refugees.
relationships.quote: we must both reassure Pakistan and encourage it to help the rebels

relationships.detail: Brzezinski is writing from the White House and refers to the upcoming NSC meeting for which he will send an agenda.
relationships.quote: I will be sending you separately a proposed agenda for the NSC meeting on Friday

relationships.detail: SCC minutes on Afghanistan and Iran are provided to the President.
relationships.quote: you are receiving today's SCC minutes on both subjects.

relationships.detail: The Soviet Union intervened militarily in Afghanistan, which the memo says could become a Soviet Vietnam.
relationships.quote: the Soviet intervention in Afghanistan poses for us an extremely grave challenge

relationships.detail: Moscow's age-long dream of direct access to the Indian Ocean would be fulfilled if the Soviets succeed in Afghanistan and Pakistan acquiesces.
relationships.quote: the age-long dream of Moscow to have direct access to the Indian Ocean will have been fulfilled.

relationships.detail: Pakistan could be intimidated and acquiesce to Soviet domination unless the US projects confidence and power.
relationships.quote: Pakistan, unless we somehow manage to project both confidence and power into the region, is likely to be intimidated

relationships.detail: Soviet-sponsored actions in Cambodia are noted alongside Afghanistan as unrestrained assertiveness; they have taken a toll.
relationships.quote: Soviet-sponsored actions in Cambodia have alreaiy taken their toll as well.

relationships.detail: The Chinese will note Soviet assertiveness in Afghanistan and Cambodia and are concerned by Soviet activity near their border.
relationships.quote: the Chinese are doubtless going to be most concerned about implications for themselves of such Soviet assertiveness so close to their border.

relationships.detail: Some 300,000 Afghan refugees are already in Pakistan; Pakistan is to be encouraged to help the rebels.
relationships.quote: There are already 300,000 refugees from Afghanistan in Pakistan

relationships.detail: Brzezinski recommends encouraging Pakistan to help the rebels, implying a support role.
relationships.quote: we must both reassure Pakistan and encourage it to help the rebels.

relationships.detail: Brzezinski recommends more money, arms shipments and technical advice to the rebels from the US.
relationships.quote: This means more money as well as arms shipments to the rebels, and some technical advice

relationships.detail: Recommends encouraging the Chinese to help the rebels.
relationships.quote: We should encourage the Chinese to help the rebels also;

relationships.detail: Proposes more guarantees and more arms aid to Pakistan, putting security policy above nonproliferation.
relationships.quote: more guarantees to it, more arms aid, and, alas, a decision that our security policy toward Pakistan cannot be dictated by our nonproliferation policy

relationships.detail: A planned Brown visit to China is referenced as being influenced by the Soviet action.
relationships.quote: will also influence the substance of the Brown visit to China

relationships.detail: Proposes taking Soviet actions in Afghanistan to the UN as a threat to peace.
relationships.quote: we should consider taking Soviet actions in Afghanistan to the UN as a threat to peace.

relationships.detail: The rebels are in Afghanistan, described as badly organized and poorly led, with no sanctuary.
relationships.quote: They have no sanctuary, no organized army, and no central government

key_claims: Brzezinski framed the Soviet intervention as a regional crisis that could give Moscow access to the Indian Ocean.
He judged Afghanistan might become a Soviet Vietnam but cautioned the resistance was badly organized, lacked sanctuary and had limited foreign support.
He recommended more money, arms and technical advice for the Afghan rebels.
He urged reassuring Pakistan with guarantees and arms aid even at the expense of nonproliferation policy.
He proposed encouraging China and Islamic countries to help the rebels, including covert action and propaganda campaigns.
He recommended warning the Soviets that SALT was at risk and raising the intervention at the UN.
